FINDINGS:

Fluid:
Small joint effusion with synovitis. Large complex popliteal cyst measuring up to 65 mm with an 11 mm osseous body in the superior aspect of the cyst. Sliver of free fluid along the inferior margin of the popliteal cyst suggesting minimal recent partial rupture.

Medial compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament, cartilage):
Moderate degenerative change.
Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal horizontal oblique component of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus with inferior surfacing. Fraying and blunting of the meniscal free edge.
Mild thickening of the proximal MCL compatible with remote injury.
Diffuse low grade partial-thickness chondral loss. Marginal osteophytosis.

Lateral compartment (meniscus, collateral ligament complex, cartilage):
Severe degenerative change with full-thickness chondral loss of the weightbearing and posterior portion of the compartment, with subchondral reactive marrow change. Marginal osteophytosis.
Complex degenerative multidirectional tear of the posterior horn extending into the body with significant maceration and substance loss of the body and anterior and posterior horn with minimal residual meniscal substance. There is some extrusion of the body of the lateral meniscus.
Thickened popliteus insertion with intrasubstance signal compatible with moderate tendinosis
Mildly thickened lateral collateral ligament proper which could reflect the sequela of a remote injury. Mild distal biceps tendinosis.

Intercondylar compartment (anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments):
Degenerative changes of the anterior cruciate ligament which remains intact. The PCL is intact.

Anterior compartment (extensor mechanism, cartilage, Hoffa's fat pad):
Mild chondropathy. Small marginal osteophytes. Mild distal quadriceps tendinosis. Mild edema at the suprapatellar fat pad.
Scarring at that the Hoffa's fat pad which could reflect the previous surgery-for clinical correlation.

Bones:
See above.

Muscles and neurovascular structures:
Normal.

Other findings:
The intra-articular body is seen at the suprapatellar joint recess on the previous MRI is no longer present.

CONCLUSION:
1.Interval worsening of the severe osteoarthritis of the lateral compartment. Complex degenerative tearing and extensive maceration the lateral meniscus.
2.Moderate degenerative change of the medial compartment. Complex degenerative tear with a dominant longitudinal oblique tear of the posterior horn and body of the medial meniscus.
3.Mild degenerative change of the patellofemoral compartment.
4.Large complex popliteal cyst with an osseous body.

MRI LEFT KNEE  (plain)

Clinical information:
Severe edema of the medial condyle of left knee.

Technique: 
Multiplanar MR of the knee according to protocol.

Comparison: 
Prior MRI dated <[Date]> of <[Month]> <[YEAR]>

Findings: 

Menisci

Lateral meniscus: Nonsurfacing hyperintensity of the posterior horn probably represents intra since degeneration. No definite meniscal tear. No para meniscal cyst.

Medial meniscus: Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface. Findings are ready seen on prior study but appears more degenerate. Several para meniscal cysts are seen at the posterior aspect of the meniscus measuring up to 0.4 cm in size. Meniscal extrusion approximately 0.6 cm noted.

Ligaments

Anterior cruciate ligament: intact

Posterior cruciate ligament: intact 

Medial collateral ligament: Superficial and deep components intact. No periligamentous edema.

Lateral collateral ligament: The iliotibial band, biceps femoris tendon, fibular collateral ligament and popliteus muscle and tendon intact. 

Posterolateral corner structures: Intact

Extensor Mechanism

The distal quadriceps and patellar tendons are intact. The patella is normally positioned within the femoral groove. There is no retinacular disruption.

Fluid

No joint effusion or loose body. Trace Baker's cyst.

Osseous and Articular Structures

Bones: A large subchondral cysts are seen at the posterior superior aspect of the tibial plateau, very much larger than prior study. Moderate degenerative changes multiple osteophytes are seen, most significant at the medial tibiofemoral joint. No fracture, stress reaction, or osseous lesion is seen.

Patellofemoral compartment: Minimal chondrosis..

Medial compartment: Focal full-thickness chondral loss measuring up to 1.3 cm in size associated subchondral edema. Moderate chondrosis in the rest of the femoral condyle Findings have slightly progressed compared to prior study.

Lateral compartment: Mild chondral irregularity. No significant subchondral edema.

Others:

Hoffas fat pad: clear

Muscles: No abnormal oedema. 

Neurovascular bundle: Normal 


COMMENT
Oblique tear of the body and posterior horn of the medial meniscus with extension to the inferior articular surface, similar to previous. Interval increase in degenerative changes of the meniscus is observed. Meniscal extrusion of approximately 0.6 cm is seen. Multiple para meniscal cysts are also present.

Interval increase in degenerative changes are identified evident as shown by increased osteophytes, full-thickness chondral loss at the medial tibiofemoral joint associated increasing subchondral edema, and multiple enlarging subchondral cysts at the posterior medial tibial plateau.

Antecedentes Clínicos:
Obs. Lesión meniscal medial.
Hallazgos:
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la médula ósea.
Aumento de señal difuso del LCA, sin signos que sugieran rotura categórica. LCP y ligamentos
colaterales dentro de límites normales.
Meniscos de morfología y señal conservada, sin criterios categóricos de rotura.
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial. El
resto de los cartílagos femorotibiales y patelofemoral sin alteraciones.
No hay significativo derrame articular ni quistes poplíteos.
Leve aumento de señal del tercio proximal del tendón rotuliano, sin signos de rotura. Tendón
cuadricipital, tendones de la pata de ganso, bíceps femoral y banda iliotibial dentro de límites
normales.
No hay alteraciones de señal significativas de la grasa de Hoffa.
Impresión:
Condropatía superficial de la región central de la zona de carga del cóndilo femoral medial.
Leve tendinosis rotuliana proximal

LEFT KNEE MRI 

CLINICAL INDICATION: Medial meniscus injury, query MCL tear

Technique: Multiplanar PD, PF fat sat and T1 imaging was acquired through the knee. 

Comparison: The x-ray [Date]

Findings:

General:
Marrow:  There is edema of the medial femoral condyle at the site of the MCL insertion, and in the posterolateral femoral condyle. There is edema in the medial proximal tibia and the posterolateral proximal tibia.
Consistent with internal bone contusion secondary valgus injury.
Effusion:  No significant effusion

Menisci:   
Medial meniscus:   Intact.
Lateral meniscus:   Intact.

Ligaments and tendons:
Cruciate ligaments:   There is increased signal in the PCL, which may be keeping with a low-grade tear. No tibial translation.
Medial collateral ligament:   High-grade partial-thickness tear of the proximal of the mid fibers of the superficial medial collateral ligament. Low-grade partial-thickness tear of the meniscal femoral as well as posterior plate components of the deep medial collateral ligament.
Lateral collateral ligament:   normal
Popliteofibular ligament:   normal
Other posterolateral corner ligaments:   normal
Popliteal tendon:   normal
Iliotibial band:   normal

Extensor mechanism:
Quadriceps tendon: Mild increased signal along the patellar insertion, in keeping with tendinosis
Patella:   normal
Patellar tendon:   normal
Hoffa?s fat pad: Subtle edema in keeping with impingement

Cartilage:
Patellofemoral joint: Mild chondrosis mainly along the trochlear aspect there
Medial compartment:   normal cartilage
Lateral compartment:  Mild chondrosis.

CONCLUSION:

1. Intact menisci.
2. High-grade partial thickness tear of the medial collateral ligament and bone contusions posterior lateral femoral condyle and lateral tibial plateau in keeping with valgus injury.
3. Mild chondrosis.
4. Mild quadriceps tendinosis without tear.

Findings:  Minor thickening of the proximal MCL with no surrounding edema suggestive of previous injury and healing with scarring. Intact lateral collateral ligament and cruciate ligaments. Small 10 mm x 12 mm x 9 mm loculated ganglion cyst adjacent to the tibial attachment of the PCL.  On a background of severe mucoid degeneration the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is severely attenuated in keeping with complex degenerate tearing, with a few small parameniscal cysts along the lateral joint line. Intact medial meniscus.  Normal appearance of the pes anserine tendons, popliteus tendon, distal biceps femoris tendon and distal iliotibial band.  Prominent enthesopathy at the superior pole of the patella at the quadriceps tendon incision. Normal patella tendon.  Low-grade chondral thinning in the lateral tibiofemoral compartment. Focal 2 mm x 2 mm low-grade cartilage defect in the weightbearing portion of the medial femoral condyle. Otherwise well maintained medial tibiofemoral hyaline articular cartilage. Relatively well-maintained patellofemoral hyaline articular cartilage.  
Conclusion:  Minor thickening of the proximal MCL with no surrounding edema suggestive of previous injury and healing with scarring. On a background of severe mucoid degeneration the body and posterior horn of the lateral meniscus is severely attenuated in keeping with complex degenerate tearing, with a few small parameniscal cysts along the lateral joint line. Ancillary findings described above.

Findings:  No significant knee effusion. Normal medial and lateral menisci. No evidence of tears.  Normal ACL, PCL, MCL and LCL. Normal extensor mechanism.  The tibiofemoral articular cartilage is preserved. Moderate - severe thinning of the lateral patellofemoral articular cartilage is noted with mild lateral patellar facet. Underlying bony change.  
Conclusion: Lateral patellofemoral degenerate change. No meniscal injury.

Knochen: Kein Bone Bruise der erfassten knöchernen Strukturen. Zentrierte Stellung im Kniegelenk. Geringe Signalanhebung innerhalb der Eminentia intercondylaris (4/15) sowie am medialen Tibiaplateau. Geringe subchondrale Zystenbildung der retropatellaren Gelenkfläche an der lateralen und medialen Facette sowie am Patellafirst. Gering osteophytäre Ausziehungen der Femurkondylen bds. bei medial betonter Gelenkspaltverschmälerung, minimale osteophytäre Ausziehungen am Tibiaplateau.
Knorpel: Ausgedehnter Knorpelbesatz an der medialen Facette der Patella mit lokal bis tiefergreifende Chondropathie. Gering ausgedünnter Knorpelbesatz der Trochlea. Bekannt höhergradige Chondropathie mit langstreckig aufgebrauchtem Knorpelbelag der medialen femoralen Kondyle (6/10) ohne Eindeutig assoziiertes Ödem Signal. Fokal bis tiefergreifende Chondropathie am Tibiaplateau medialseitig. Lateral oberflächliche Chondropathie, keine tief greifende Läsion des Knorpelbesatz des.
Menisci: 
Diffuse Signalanhebung des Innenmeniskus Hinterhornes ohne Rissbildung, in erster Linie mukoide Degeneration. Horizontale Rissbildung des Außenmeniskusvorderhornes bis in die Pars intermedia und in das Hinterhorn (5/25). Keine parameniskalen Zysten, keine Herniation.
Kapsel/Sehnen/Bänder: Intakte Darstellung des HKB und VKB. Das VKB imponiert im Verlauf gering aufgefasert und signalangehoben ohne jedoch vollständige Diskontinuität. Reizzustand des medialen Kollateralbandes. Mediales und laterales Kollateralband intakt ohne Läsion. Intakte Darstellung der Quadrizepssehne und Patellasehne.
Gelenkkapsel nicht verdickt, kein wesentlicher Erguss. Keine freien Gelenkkörper. 
Fettkörper: Kein raumfordernder Prozess, unauffällig.
Gefäß-Nervenbündel: Unauffällig. 
Subkutanes Weichgewebe/Muskulatur: Unauffällig.
